..
Issued at 342 AM CDT Wed Jul 22 2026

Slightly warmer yet near normal temperatures in the 80s will be
found today as a surface high exits the east and northwest flow
remains aloft. Light winds will become a light southerly wind 
today, bringing the slightly warmer temperatures. A lack of 
instability and lift will also bring a mainly dry forecast for 
today. HRRR Smoke showing perhaps some low amounts of smoke 
lingering today, although should diminish as winds become 
southerly. For now kept smoke mention out of the forecast. 
Patchy fog this morning and again Thursday morning should also 
be limited as model soundings showing mostly dry air still in 
place. Overnight lows tonight will generally be in the mid 50s
to lower 60s. Above normal temperatures in the upper 80s to mid
90s then look to return for Thursday as southerly flow 
increases and a westerly to northwesterly flow pattern is found 
aloft. A weak disturbance may bring some showers and 
thunderstorms across the south, although most of this 
precipitation is expected to remain in SD. Meanwhile, some weak 
instability and a favorable entrance region of the upper jet 
across the north could bring a few isolated showers and 
thunderstorms across the north Thursday afternoon. The overall 
threat for severe weather is low on Thursday. Any lingering
precipitation should diminish Thursday evening. Lows Thursday
night will be mild and generally in the 60s. Another developing
disturbance could bring some showers and thunderstorms to the
northwest late Thursday night into early Friday morning. 

Friday, surface trough looks to move across the state with
strong heating expected across much of the CWA. High
temperatures look to return into the 90s to lower 100s for most
areas. Afternoon humidity values in the teens and 20s across the
southwest, combined with a breezy westerly wind could bring near
critical to perhaps critical fire weather conditions. Meanwhile,
slightly improved dewpoints in the north and east could provide
for more instability and increased chances for showers and
thunderstorms in these areas on Friday. SPC did clip parts of
the James River Valley in a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 5) for
severe weather on Friday, while the CSU-MLP severe forecast also
showing the potential for isolated severe storms across much of
ND. Shear is modest to high for Friday, although instability is
only adequate for stronger storms. There is also going to be 
some capping to overcome with the warming aloft expected on 
Friday. However, if storms can develop in our CWA strong winds 
and large hail would be the main threats. SPC mentions surface 
based storms have favorable hodographs for a tornado or two as 
well, although confidence in surface based storms remains 
uncertain at this time. Heat products may be needed starting as 
early as Friday, with Heat Index values near 100 degrees. 
Saturday still looks to be the hotter day with highs 95 to 105. 
Gulf moisture still looks to be cut off for Saturday, with dry 
air aloft likely mixing down to the surface. The result could be
even lower afternoon humidity values in the teens and 20s for 
most areas. The building high pressure should limit winds on 
Saturday, as well as the fire weather threat. Current forecast 
has some isolated thunderstorm chances Saturday, although 
instability looks limited at this time. Even with a more dry 
heat on Saturday, heat products may again be needed as well. Hot
temperatures and perhaps some increased northwest winds from a 
weak surface low could bring another day of near critical fire 
weather conditions on Sunday. Even with dry air continuing to 
linger, some heat products may again be needed for Sunday. 
Instability looks limited again on Sunday, although the 
mentioned weak surface low could provide for some isolated 
thunderstorm chances. Models indicating the ridge trying to 
flatten early next week, although uncertainty remains on just 
how much weakening can happen. Current forecast has slightly 
cooler yet still well above normal temperatures as a result of 
this potential flattening. Isolated to perhaps scattered 
thunderstorms are possible if any ridge riding waves can move 
through, which would once again depend on how much flattening 
occurs. Low RH values also look to continue into early next 
week, which could continue to linger at least some increased 
fire weather concerns.
